negative: extra hands, duplicate hands, third arm, floating disembodied hands, extra head, duplicate head
light sources inside boats, candles in illogical places, skeletons with light sources
body parts fused into walls or stone, hands or limbs protruding from architecture, figures merged with stonework, disembodied hands emerging from surfaces

people looking at something in the background must be shown from behind or in profile, facing into the frame toward it; never show faces and have them looking at a background element simultaneously; eyeline must match camera position
objects defying gravity, swords balancing on their points, items floating or suspended in mid-air unsupported
disembodied hands emerging from clothing, sleeves, furniture, or floors; hands with no attached body
figures partially sunk into or emerging from floors or paving; people must stand fully on top of the ground, whole bodies visible, never embedded in the floor
incorrect object counts; when a specific number of objects is named, render exactly that number, never more or fewer
phantom or floating hands in empty scenes; scenes specified as empty must contain zero human body parts of any kind
in scenes requiring no people, frame tightly on objects or surfaces so there is no space a figure could occupy; absolutely no hands, fingers, or limbs anywhere in the frame
split-screen compositions are forbidden; never combine interior and exterior in one frame; pick one location and stay in it

AI image models cannot reliably render small text, engravings, or inscriptions legibly; always frame text-bearing objects so the writing is partially obscured, in shadow, at an oblique angle, or outside the depth of focus; never rely on the model to produce specific legible words on objects

for any recurring character or recurring ensemble across multiple shots, embed the full canonical visual description into every prompt where they appear; do not assume the model remembers earlier shots; consistency must be enforced shot by shot
motion_rules: PEOPLE ARE THE EMOTIONAL CORE. Most shots should include human figures — the families, the crowds at a distance, individuals reacting. Do NOT default to empty rooms and landscapes. Empty atmospheric shots are the exception, not the rule.

Avoid shots where a hand manipulates an object on screen (closing a shutter, opening a door). Hands warp badly in motion. Show the RESULT instead — a shutter already closed, a door already shut, ash already settled on the sill.
Avoid close side-on shots of animals; image models hallucinate their anatomy. Frame animals small, distant, in shadow, or partially obscured.

Keep faces near-static in MOTION (to avoid warping when animated), but DO show people clearly in the still. Animate the environment (ash, smoke, water, light) around a still or barely-moving figure rather than animating the face itself.
No fast action, no running, no combat, no crowds in fast motion. Slow and atmospheric only.
